- Avoid over-forecasting in early periods after a spike; model tends to overshoot and then correct, but often undercorrects in the first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00), model should not assume strong directional bias; instead, anchor forecast to recent mean or median of 10–15 day window.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend after a low, model often underreacts — increase forecast slope slightly in next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast peaks too early or too high after a spike, reduce peak by 2–5% and shift peak forward by 1–3 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon — if model forecasts a sharp move, adjust downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- In absence of sentiment signal, model should not assume momentum — use 15-day rolling average as baseline for correction.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >3% in 3–5 days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 5–7 days) — increase forecast by 1–2% in final 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly positive.
